name: invalid_integrator_bounds_fails_init
description: limMinInt > limMaxInt is a nonsensical configuration -- the anti-windup clamp in PID.c would run backwards. pid_fmi2.c checks this at fmi2ExitInitializationMode and refuses to initialize, logging the reason through the FMU's own logger. THIS SCENARIO IS EXPECTED TO FAIL: running it should return ok=false with error code 'fmi_call_failed' (or, from the plain CLI, exit code 2 with the FMU's log message), not a crash and not a silent wrong answer. It demonstrates the runner's error-handling path on a real native rejection, distinct from a failed numeric check.

metadata.derived_from: src/pid_fmi2.c fmi2ExitInitializationMode, the limMinInt/limMaxInt validity check
